newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anti-nukes plan Clinton protest on Sydney Harbour.
newsitem.headline: Anti-nukes plan Clinton protest on Sydney Harbour.

text.p: Anti-nuclear demonstrators in inflatable craft plan to harrass U.S. President Bill Clinton during his Sydney Harbour cruise with Australia's prime minister on Wednesday evening, a spokesman for the protest group said.
"We are taking two of our inflatable boats, with loudhailers whistles and placards, out to shadow the president and prime minister on Sydney Harbour," said Robert Samsa of the Sydney Peace Squadron.
The group staged a noisy daylight protest when then U.S. president George Bush toured the landmark harbour in 1992.
Samsa said protesters planned to stay on the harbour for the full two hour cruise and make their views known to Clinton and Australian Prime Minister John Howard.
"We will get as close as security will let us, but I don't think we will be able to get too close," Samsa told Reuters.
"We are not as fast as the police boats, but we are more manoeuvrable. We are only taking three people in the inflatables which will mean we should be able to out-manoeuvre the security."

Samsa said saftey was a priority and both protest craft would be carrying lights. "It is very dangerous to be on Sydney Harbour at night without lights and there will be lots of boats out there tonight," he said.
Samsa said the squadron was protesting the United States' policy of maintaining nuclear weapons and its decision not to declare an intention to abolish nuclear weapons for good.
Clinton and his wife Hillary arrived in Australia on Tuesday for a five-day visit taking in Sydney, Canberra and tropical Queensland state.
